newsitem.title: IRAN: Khatami says Iran will not disrupt Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Khatami says Iran will not disrupt Mideast peace.

text.p: Iran's president-elect Mohammad Khatami said on Tuesday the Islamic republic opposed the Middle East peace process but would not take any action to disrupt it.

"...Regarding the so-called Middle East peace process, we do believe that there will be no possibility for any peace to be established except with the restoration of the legal rights of all Palestinian people," Khatami told a news conference.
"We are interested in peace and tranquility...under the condition that the rights of all sides to the matter would be observed," he told his first news conference since his victory in Friday's polls.
Iran rejects Israeli and U.S. accusations it supported Islamic militants opposed to the peace process and says it only gave political support to groups opposed to peace.
The Islamic republic condemns the peace process between Israel and its Arab neighbours as a sell-out of Palestinian rights.

"Of course, we are not going to have any intervention in this matter and we are going to leave it to the people of Palestine and the governments and the people of the region," said Khatami, who takes over as president in August.
"But we do keep the right to express our views regarding the matter...and with a scientific, realistic approach we do think that the current process will not come to any conclusion."
